description: To introduce the importance, concepts and components of computer integrated manufacturing.

syllabus.title: Introduction; Manufacturing Systems
syllabus.body: Introduction: Introduction to manufacturing enterprise, External and internal changes, World-class winning criteria, Introduction to CIM concepts, Three step process for CIM implementation. Manufacturing Systems: Manufacturing classifications, Product development cycle, Enterprise organization.

syllabus.title: Design Automation; Manufacturing Planning and Control
syllabus.body: Design Automation: Computer-Aided Design and Engineering: Introduction, General system operation, CAD classification: Hardware and software platforms, Application of CAD to manufacturing systems, Design for manufacturing and assembly, Computer-aided engineering analysis and evaluation. Manufacturing Planning and Control: Introduction, planning the manufacturing planning and control system, master production schedule, inventory management, product data management.

syllabus.title: Material Planning, Production Scheduling and Operating Systems; Enterprise Resource Planning
syllabus.body: Material Planning, Production Scheduling and Operating Systems: Material requirement planning, Capacity requirement planning, MRP II, Just-in-time manufacturing. Enterprise Resource Planning: MRP II – a driver of effective ERP systems, information technology, the decision to implement ERP system, Features of modern manufacturing planning and control systems.

syllabus.title: Production Support Machines and Systems; Machine and System Control
syllabus.body: Production Support Machines and Systems: Industrial robots, automated material handling systems, automated guided vehicles, automated storage and retrieval systems. Machine and System Control: System overview, Cell control, Proprietary versus Open system interconnect software, Device control, programmable logic controllers, Computer numerical control, Automatic tracking, Network communications.

outcomes: To understand CIM and its scope
To understand product design and manufacturing in CIM environment
To understand manufacturing planning and control in CIM environment
To understand hardware and software requirements for CIM as well as implementation of CIM
textbooks: Computer-integrated manufacturing, James A. Rehg and Henry W. Kraebber, Pearson Education.
Computer Integrated Manufacturing Technology and Systems, U. Rembolt, C. Blume, R. Dillmann, Dekker,
Computer Integrated Design and Manufacturing, D.D. Bedworth, M.R. Henderson, P.M. Wolfe, McGraw Hill.
Systems Approach to Computer Integrated Design and Manufacturing, N. Singh, John Wiley & Sons.
Automation Production Systems and Computer Integrated Manufacturing, M.P. Groover, Pearson
